t1_transform.design: 4x4 integer Hadamard on luma, fixed zigzag truncation, uniform step with a coarser DC step, one Co/Cg pair per chroma cell; no significance mask so coefficient i of sub-block j is at a computable offset

native.transform: 4x4 integer Hadamard on luma, fixed zigzag truncation, uniform step, one Co/Cg pair per 4x4
native.accounting: Payload record bytes only. Descriptor and addressing bits are identical for both families and are excluded, which favours neither.
native.interpretation: Intra comparison on source blocks. Palette modes are intra, so this is the like-for-like question; temporal compact classes are not covered and are reported separately.

t1_transform.verdict: Beaten by the existing palette modes at every block size and byte budget on the benchmark proxy. Competitive on natural video only above roughly 40 bytes per 8x8 block, an order of magnitude above the 2.2 to 15.2 logical bytes per 32x32 block the ladder actually spends.

t2_entropy.scheme: Static canonical Huffman per payload category over byte values, fixed-size chunks with a 16-bit offset and 4-bit selector each.
t2_entropy.admissibility: No frame-wide serial dependency: a fragment walks at most one chunk. Arithmetic and CABAC-style coding across the frame stay inadmissible.
t2_entropy.verdict: The rate win is real at 20.8% of payload per record and 24.4% chunked, but a fragment loses random access inside a record and GPU fragments run in lockstep, so the worst-case record length is what is paid. Only palette patterns and solid colours, 14.1% of the payload, have worst-case records inside the 2x ceiling, and coding just those nets 1.9% of the map rate.

assumptions: Static per-category tables ship in the resource pack and are not charged, like the existing colour codebooks; cross-content generalization of those tables is untested.
The walk cost is a synthetic dependent-lookup chain, not a decoder, so a real Huffman decoder adds bit-shift work on top and the figures are floors.
Worst-case walk assumes a subgroup contains one fragment covering the longest record of its category, which is what lockstep execution implies.
Nothing here is implemented in the codec and no figure is an attained map rate.
verdict: Neither path is worth pursuing inside the vanilla shader constraints. The transform is the wrong tool for this content at the byte budgets the ladder uses, and entropy coding trades away the per-fragment random access the format exists to provide. The binding constraint on this format is random access, not the six-bit transport or the syntax.
